# Amazon Deforestation Drivers (2010-2020)
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
Between 2010 and 2020, deforestation in the Amazon rainforest was primarily driven by human activities aimed at economic gain, leading to significant loss of biodiversity and carbon sinks.

## Key Causes and Contributing Sectors
The main factors contributing to the destruction of the Amazon during this period were deeply intertwined with agricultural expansion, resource extraction, and infrastructure development.

| Primary Cause | Contributing Industries | Description                                                                                             |
| :------------ | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Cattle Ranching | Livestock (Beef, Leather) | The single largest driver, clearing vast areas for pasture to meet global demand for beef and related products. |
| Agriculture     | Soy, Palm Oil, other crops | Expansion of large-scale commercial farming, particularly for soybean cultivation, often for animal feed.     |
| Illegal Logging | Timber Industry         | Unregulated and unsustainable harvesting of valuable timber species, often facilitated by new road access.  |
| Mining          | Gold, Other Minerals    | Both legal and illegal mining operations for gold and other minerals, leading to habitat destruction and pollution. |
| Infrastructure  | Construction, Energy    | Development of new roads, hydroelectric dams, and energy projects, opening up previously inaccessible forest areas. |
| Forest Fires    | Various (Land Clearing) | Often intentionally set to clear land for agriculture or ranching, these fires frequently spread uncontrollably. |
